headline: HIV-Positive Patient Gets Kidney in Days Through New Transplant Program
meta_description: An HIV-positive patient who waited over two years for a kidney received one in less than a week after joining Cedars Sinai's new HIV-to-HIV transplant program.
summary_short: After more than two years of waiting, an HIV-positive patient received a kidney transplant in less than a week through Cedars Sinai's groundbreaking new program.
body:
An HIV-positive patient who had waited more than two years for a kidney received an organ in less than a week after joining a new HIV-to-HIV transplant program at Cedars Sinai.

The program represents a significant shift in transplant medicine, expanding the pool of available organs by matching HIV-positive donors with HIV-positive recipients. This approach challenges long-standing restrictions that historically prevented people with HIV from donating organs, even to others living with the virus.

For patients like this one at Cedars Sinai, the impact is transformative. The dramatic reduction in wait time—from years to days—offers hope to many HIV-positive people facing organ failure while on transplant waiting lists.
quick_facts: HIV-positive patient received kidney in under one week
Previously waited more than two years for transplant
Cedars Sinai launched new HIV-to-HIV transplant program
Program matches HIV-positive donors with HIV-positive recipients
